issues.description: The verify command 'microk8s kubectl create clusterrolebinding test --clusterrole=pod-reader --user=jane --dry-run=server 2>&1' uses --clusterrole, which means it attempts to create a valid ClusterRoleBinding referencing a ClusterRole. This does NOT demonstrate the error scenario described in the question, which is binding a namespaced Role (not a ClusterRole) via a ClusterRoleBinding. The command would succeed (or fail only because 'pod-reader' ClusterRole doesn't exist), not because of the Role-vs-ClusterRole mismatch that the question tests.
issues.suggested_fix: Change verify to a command that demonstrates the actual error, e.g.: kubectl create clusterrolebinding test --clusterrole=nonexistent-role --user=jane --dry-run=server 2>&1  OR add a comment explaining that the kubectl CLI does not support --role for clusterrolebinding, so the error must be demonstrated via a YAML manifest with roleRef.kind set to Role.

issues.description: The verify command 'kubectl get --raw /healthz/encrypt' references a non-existent API server endpoint. There is no '/healthz/encrypt' health check endpoint in Kubernetes. The encryption-at-rest configuration does not expose a dedicated healthz sub-path.
issues.suggested_fix: Change verify to: kubectl get apiserver -o=jsonpath='{.spec.encryption}' --all-namespaces  OR  ps aux | grep kube-apiserver | grep encryption-provider-config  OR  kubectl -n kube-system get pod kube-apiserver-<node> -o yaml | grep encryption-provider-config

issues.description: The verify jsonpath uses '?(@.name=="kube-api-access")' but the actual projected volume name in Kubernetes includes a random hash suffix (e.g., 'kube-api-access-abc12'). The exact-match filter will not match any volume, returning an empty result.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a broader approach: kubectl get pod <pod> -o yaml | grep -A10 serviceAccountToken  OR use a jsonpath that doesn't rely on exact volume name matching: kubectl get pod <pod> -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumes[*].projected.sources[*].serviceAccountToken.expirationSeconds}'

issues.description: The verify command 'helm template <chart> --dry-run=server 2>&1' is incorrect. The 'helm template' command renders charts locally and does not support '--dry-run=server'. The --dry-run flag on 'helm template' does not accept 'server' as a value. Furthermore, 'helm template' never contacts the Kubernetes API, so lookup functions always return empty data during template rendering. To actually test lookup behavior against a live cluster, you need 'helm install' or 'helm upgrade' with --dry-run=server.
issues.suggested_fix: Change verify to: helm install test-release <chart> --dry-run=server 2>&1  (this contacts the API server and exercises lookup functions while not actually installing)
